l.i: Chronologia est ars tempora recte distinguendi.

main_text.l: I. ÆC Chronologiæ ἀπὸ τῆ͂ς χρόνου
nequit. Nam ἡ μὲν ἀεὶ ἐπιστήμη
ἔστι ἐξεις ἀποδεικτικὴ, Scientia est habitus
demonstrationis, ut ait philosophus, Ethic. l. 6. c. 3. Talis
nimirum habitus, quo quippiam nobis sit demonstratum, adeo
ut de eo quodammodo certi simus. ὅταν γὰρ πιστεύω,

page.notes: The page is a title page with a woodcut frieze above the title lines; the frieze carries no text. The page number I is printed at the top right. The scan is cut off below the title, so the remainder of the page is not included here. The Greek and Hebrew inline are rendered approximately; the woodcut initial H is joined to the first word. Several Greek words in the first lines are uncertain and marked by their approximate form only.
